page.layout: Running head at top, with page number at top left. Below it, two round portrait medallions side by side, each with a legend around its edge. Below them, one full-width column of text in two paragraphs. Below the text, a woodcut ornament with no text. No margin notes.

main_text.l: CAROLUS RUINUS REGIENSIS.
FRANC. CURTIUS PAPIENSIS.
CAROLVS Ruinus, Regiensis Iurisconsultus inter alios
celebris & magni nominis, qui ius Bononię docuit, tanto iudi-
cio, ut ęqualem aliis doctioribus Iuris professoribus, gloria com-
parauerit. Indefessus fuit in obeundo munere, & plures disci-
pulos habuit, à quibus & amatus est & summe reueritus. Scri-
psit super prima & secunda Digesti noui. Item Consiliorum vo-
lumina quinque impressa Venetiis & Lugduni. Floruit anno re-
paratę salutis humanę 1520. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, & li-
brum, De vita Iurisconsultorum.
FRANCISCVS Curtius Iurisconsultus clarissimus
extitit, qui de iure itidem multa scripsit ad communem eorum
utilitatem qui legibus dant operam. Scripsit super C. in tit. de
iura. calumnię. Fecit additiones ad Practicam Ioannis Petri de
Ferrariis. De moneta super 2. ff. veteris, si certum petatur, l.cum
quid. Super 1. C. de prohib. seq. pecun. lege prima, Quoties.
De sequestris. De testibus. Consiliorum volumen unum. Et plu-
rima alia usui forensi accommodata. Franciscus Curtius Iunior,
Papiensis ius etiam professus est, ut scriptis declarauit plurimis.
Scripsit enim super 1. & 2. ff. veteris. De feudis. Consiliorum vo-
lumen. &c. Florebant anno. 1533. Vide Conradum Gesnerum,
in sua Bibliotheca, & librum, De vita Iurisconsultorum.

page.notes: Page number at top left is hard to read; read as "2,o" with an old-style o, possibly 230 or 240 — uncertain. The running head ends with a stray mark after ICONVM, left out. Medallion legends are set in capitals; u/v normalised by vowel/consonant rule (RVINVS to RUINUS, CVRTIVS to CURTIUS). Both medallion legends are transcribed as printed lines before the text. Italic run-in names in the paragraphs are marked with <i>, as the names look spaced/capitalised rather than italic; this is a best guess.
